docs.html:
1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to when a participant needs behaviour support urgently, before a full assessment is possible. It is for participants, their families and advocates, the providers who support them, our and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every participant we are asked to help, or find, who has an for behaviour support. This includes a participant whose providers are using, or are likely to use, a that no behaviour support plan covers.
  • Every Practitioner, , manager and worker of [Provider name], contractors included, who takes part in an interim plan.
  • Every setting: the participant's own home, a shared home, a day service, a school, a hospital or the community.
  • Specialist behaviour support only. A provider that only implements plans uses POL-BSP-08 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Policy (Implementing Behaviour Support Plans).

3Commitments

C1

We will decide the urgency of every referral within 1 , using the bands in PRO-SBS-06. A referral that is not an immediate need goes to the right pathway the same day, and we tell the referrer why.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 2, Procedure step 3, Procedure step 4.

C2

We will answer in writing every referral that needs an interim plan. For danger now we answer the same business day, and for urgent within 2 business days. If we cannot take it, we say so in that time and help the referrer find another specialist behaviour support provider.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 5, Procedure step 6, Procedure step 7.

C3

We will put safety first. Where anyone is in danger now, we tell the referrer to call 000 before we ask anything else. We check what keeps people safe until the plan is . We do this on the day we accept for danger now, and within 1 business day for urgent.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 1, Procedure step 9.

C4

We will use only a Practitioner, an NDIS behaviour support practitioner whom the Commissioner considers suitable, to evaluate the risk and write the plan. That includes any contractor we engage. A Clinical Supervisor checks every interim plan before it is issued.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 5, Procedure step 26.

C5

We will record an on the day we accept a referral. We will issue the interim plan within 5 business days of it for danger now, and within 10 for urgent. Where a regulated restrictive practice is involved, we will never issue it later than 1 month after the engagement date. We will issue the comprehensive plan within 6 months of it; 84 days is our target. An interim plan's review date is the comprehensive plan's due date, never 12 months. The Service Manager checks every open plan against these dates at least every week.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 7, Procedure step 8, Procedure step 27, Procedure step 35, Procedure step 37.

C6

We will involve the participant in evaluating the risk, in the way they choose. We show them the draft plan before it is final. We give them their copy in a form they can use, and we explain it. We do this within 1 business day of issuing the plan, and before we tell anyone else.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 10, Procedure step 11, Procedure step 12, Procedure step 24, Procedure step 28.

C7

We will involve every provider that carries out the participant's supports in evaluating the risk and in considering the draft plan. We also take account of earlier assessments, and of what family, carers and other services tell us, with the participant's consent.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 11, Procedure step 13, Procedure step 14, Procedure step 25.

C8

We will evaluate the risk the behaviour poses to the participant and to others, and what may be driving it, before we write any strategy. We rate each risk and record it.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 12, Procedure step 13, Procedure step 15, Procedure step 16, Procedure step 17.

C9

We will write each interim plan on the Commissioner's approved form, or on another form that section 23(1) of allows and that holds every required item. Its content follows the Commission's Interim Behaviour Support Plan Checklist (October 2025): it is brief and usable; it evaluates the risk of harm; it does not include a functional behaviour assessment; it sets out changes within the environment; for any restrictive practice it says what is used, when, why, how and by whom; and it says how advice, and support will be given. Its strategies are evidence-based, person-centred and proactive. They address the participant's needs and the likely reason for the behaviour, and give the participant chances to build skills and join in community life.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 15, Procedure step 22, Procedure step 23, Procedure step 26, Procedure step 27.

C10

We will include a regulated restrictive practice in an interim plan only if it is authorised, or is on the state or territory's interim or short term pathway, and the plan identifies it clearly and states its authorisation status. Where authorisation is not yet in place, the plan says the practice must not be used, and says what happens until authorisation is granted. The plan also says how the practice will be reduced and ended. It must also meet every test in the Rules: last resort, least restrictive, in proportion to the risk and for the shortest time. We never include a practice that the state or territory prohibits.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 18, Procedure step 19, Procedure step 20.

C11

We will give the participant, and their family, carers, guardian or other relevant person, the details of any intention to include a restrictive practice. We do this in a format they can use, before the plan is final.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 21.

C12

We will every interim plan that contains a regulated restrictive practice with the Commissioner within 5 business days of finalising it. We lodge it whether or not authorisation is in place.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 29.

C13

We will give each the issued plan and its point-of-care card, and brief its manager, within 1 business day of issuing the plan. We complete the handover, training and guidance within the interim handover clock in PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure: 2 business days from issue. We check that they can follow it. Only with the participant's consent, we give the same guidance to their in the same time.

Answers: Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 11, Procedure step 30, Procedure step 31.

C14

We will check how the plan is working within 7 days of issuing it. After that we check it at least every 1 month, as PRO-SBS-04 sets. We review the plan early when it is not working. When the need is over, we replace the plan with a comprehensive plan or close it, and record why.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 32, Procedure step 33, Procedure step 34, Procedure step 35, Procedure step 36, Procedure step 37.

4Ground rules

G1

This policy and every interim plan authorise no regulated restrictive practice. Only the authorisation process of the state or territory can do that, where it has one.

G2

Safety comes before paperwork. Nobody holds back a safety step while a service agreement or funding is sorted out. We complete AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template alongside the work. If the participant's NDIS plan has no behaviour support funding, the Chief Executive decides whether we start the interim plan, and records the decision.

G3

An interim plan never waits for the full assessment. The functional behaviour assessment belongs to the comprehensive plan, under PRO-BSP-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure.

G4

The engagement date is the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used and led to the referral, whichever is earlier (our standard). The Commission treats a provider as engaged from the service agreement date, or a later start date the agreement names, so our date is never later than the Commission's. Our written acceptance states that it is the start date for developing the plan for the purposes of the Rules, section 19, and the service agreement (AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template) records the same date. We do not wait for a signed service agreement. PRO-BSP-03 sets the general rule.

G5

Where a regulated restrictive practice is in use or likely, we apply the 1 month and 6 month limits in section 19 of the Rules. The Rules set them where a practice has been used and we are engaged as a result. We apply them to a likely practice too. This is our standard.

G6

Nobody at [Provider name] can extend a time limit that the law sets. A late step is recorded with its reason. The dates on the register are never changed to hide it.

G7

Only a Practitioner evaluates the risk and writes the plan. Other workers, families and providers give information, records and views. No automated tool decides a risk or writes a plan on its own. A tool that helps with a draft gets only information with names and details removed. The Practitioner answers for every word (POL-TEC-01 Artificial Intelligence and Automated Tools Policy).

G8

We presume every participant can decide, with support (POL-RGT-03 Independence and Informed Choice Policy). Where another person holds legal authority, we see the order or instrument and record what it covers. We share a participant's information only as they consent, or as the law requires or allows. If consent is refused, we explain what that means, offer an independent advocate and tell the Clinical Supervisor the same day. The Practitioner goes on with the collection and consultation that the Rules require for a plan containing a restrictive practice (the Rules, section 20(3); Privacy Act 1988, Australian Privacy Principles 3 and 6, where collection or use is required or authorised by law), collects only what the plan needs, and records the refusal and what was collected despite it. The safety steps with the provider go on. The wording of this ground rule is settled once by legal advice on the template, not decided case by case.

G9

A regulated restrictive practice used without authorisation, or outside the plan, can be a reportable incident for the provider that used it. See , section 16. We support that provider under POL-SBS-06 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Policy (Specialist Behaviour Support).

G10

In a sole practitioner business, the Practitioner holds the Service Manager, , Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles and does what those roles do, with two exceptions. The external Clinical Supervisor, engaged in writing and named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, does the Service Manager's checks on the Practitioner's own work, and makes any reportable-incident decision with the Practitioner. REG-GOV-01 also names a cover Practitioner, who must be an NDIS behaviour support practitioner and is arranged in writing before they are needed, and an independent contact for concerns, who reads REG-SBS-01 every 3 months.

G11

A concern about a colleague or a manager goes to the Clinical Supervisor. A concern about the Clinical Supervisor goes to the Clinical Lead. A concern about the Service Manager or the Clinical Lead goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive goes to the chair of the governing body. Where one person owns the provider, it goes to the independent contact for concerns (POL-INC-01 Incident Management Policy, Ground rules). Nobody is punished for raising it.

G12

A participant, family member, carer or advocate can complain about an interim plan, or about how we made it. We handle it under POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy. A complaint never delays a safety step.

The result is a row in REG-QMS-02 Internal Audit Schedule and Register.

7Authority

305 words

  • NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission, Interim Behaviour Support Plan Checklist: Requirements for Specialist Behaviour Support Providers (October 2025), and the Commission's position statement on the interim and workflow (February 2026). Commission guidance, not law: the checklist sets what an auditor will look for in an interim plan, and the position statement sets when a provider is engaged and when a newly engaged provider need not write a fresh interim plan.
  • National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018, sections 6 and 8 to 10. They define a regulated restrictive practice and ban one that a state or territory prohibits. They also set authorisation and use only under a plan.
  • The Rules, sections 17 to 21: the Practitioner, the one month and six month periods, how a plan is developed and what it contains.
  • The Rules, sections 23 and 24: the approved form and lodgement with the Commissioner.
  • The Rules, sections 11 to 14: the duties of the providers who carry out the plan, which this policy supports.
  • NDIS Act 2013, sections 73F(1)(c), 73H and 73J: the Rules set conditions of registration, and breaching a condition is a contravention.
  • National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018, section 7(2). A provider must be registered where there is, or is likely to be, an interim or ongoing need to use a regulated restrictive practice.
  • The Incident Rules, section 16: when the use of a restrictive practice is a reportable incident.
  • Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), where it applies to us, and the health records and privacy law of [state or territory].
  • The guardianship law and the restrictive practice authorisation law of [state or territory].

9Words we use

436 words
the Rules
the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
the Incident Rules
the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
interim behaviour support plan
a plan written quickly to manage the risk of a participant's behaviour until a comprehensive plan replaces it.
immediate need
the participant's behaviour puts them or others at risk of harm now or soon, and no plan manages it. It also covers a regulated restrictive practice in use, or likely to be used, that no plan covers.
urgency band
the group a referral is placed in: danger now, urgent, not immediate, or covered by a current plan. PRO-SBS-06 sets them.
comprehensive behaviour support plan
the full plan that follows a behaviour support assessment and a functional behaviour assessment.
Practitioner
an NDIS behaviour support practitioner. The Commissioner considers this person suitable to do behaviour support assessments and write plans that may include restrictive practices.
Clinical Supervisor
an experienced Practitioner who checks the Practitioner's work and supports their practice.
Clinical Lead
the senior Practitioner who owns clinical practice at [Provider name].
implementing provider
a provider whose workers carry out the participant's supports and will carry out the plan.
support network
the family, carers, friends, advocates and others the participant chooses.
regulated restrictive practice
seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint or environmental restraint, as the Rules define them (the Rules, section 6). A locked cupboard is environmental. A bed rail used to stop movement is mechanical. A medicine given mainly to change behaviour is chemical.
authorisation
the permission a state or territory gives, through its own process, for a regulated restrictive practice. Some states and territories have no such process.
interim pathway
a state or territory's short term or interim authorisation route for a practice that must be used before full authorisation can be decided, where the state or territory has one.
engagement date
the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used and led to the referral, whichever is earlier. The clocks in the Rules, section 19, run from it.
lodge
send to the Commissioner, in the form and the way the Commissioner requires.
issued
finalised and in force, on the date the Practitioner signs the plan. Issued, finalised and in force mean the same date in this policy and in PRO-SBS-06.
guidance
teaching and coaching on how to carry out the plan, with a check that it was understood.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

1Purpose

The result: a participant with an for behaviour support has the risk evaluated with them and with the providers who support them. An interim plan that manages the risk is then , lodged where the law requires, and explained to the people who will carry it out.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SBS-07 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Policy, C1 to C14.

2When and who

Start this procedure when [Provider name] is told that a participant may have an immediate need for behaviour support. The news can come from an , a family member, the participant, a support coordinator, a plan manager, a hospital or the NDIS Commission. It can also come from our own . A provider may use FRM-BSP-08 Interim Behaviour Support Engagement Record to ask us.

Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this procedure. A provider that only implements plans uses PRO-BSP-09 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Implementing Behaviour Support Plans).

If PRO-BSP-03 has already logged and triaged the referral, use that record. Do not enter it again. Start at step 3, and set the target date at step 7.

Who acts:

  • Whoever takes the referral writes it down and tells the Service Manager.
  • The sets the .
  • The Service Manager answers the referral, sets the dates, the plan and keeps the clocks.
  • The Practitioner does the clinical work, from the first safety check to the close of the plan.
  • The checks the plan before it is issued.
  • The cover Practitioner takes over when the Practitioner is absent.
  • The Chief Executive is told when a legal limit will be missed.

A sole Practitioner holds the Service Manager, Clinical Lead, Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles and does what those roles do, with two exceptions. The external Clinical Supervisor named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register does the Service Manager's checks on the Practitioner's own work, and makes any reportable-incident decision with the Practitioner. Where a step says to tell another role, a sole Practitioner writes it on the plan row and tells the Clinical Supervisor.

3Before you start

  • You know the referral number: [referral phone number]. Its message tells callers to ring 000 first if anyone is in danger now.
  • You can open REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register, FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-SBS-07 Interim Behaviour Support Risk Evaluation. You know where the paper copies are kept.
  • You know who the Practitioner, the Clinical Supervisor and the cover Practitioner are. You have the suitability record kept under PRO-SBS-01 Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support).
  • You can find the schedule for the participant's state or territory in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.
  • You can get the Commissioner's current approved plan form through FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record.

4Watch out

  • Call 000 first. If anyone is in danger now, the referrer calls 000 before anything else. Our phone line cannot keep a person safe, and every question asked first costs time.
  • Do not advise a restrictive practice by phone. Advice to use one, with no plan and no authorisation, can make the provider's use unauthorised. The provider may then have to report it as a reportable incident.
  • The clock starts at engagement, not at the plan. The 1 month limit runs from the . Missing it breaches a condition of our registration (Rules, s 19(2)(a)). That can lead to a civil penalty (NDIS Act 2013, s 73J).
  • The other provider's clock may end sooner. Its 1 month limit runs from the first use of the practice. Step 8 tells it the date. The law is in the Rules, s 11(2), s 12(2) and s 13(2).
  • An interim plan does not wait for the full assessment. The functional behaviour assessment belongs to the comprehensive plan (Rules, s 20(5)). Holding the interim plan back for it leaves the risk unmanaged.
  • Never write an unauthorised practice as allowed. A worker who reads "allowed" will use it. The provider then uses a practice with no authority.
  • Sharing without consent breaches privacy. It can also put the participant at risk, for example if a family member is part of the concern.

5Steps

Take the referral

Step 1

Warning. Our phone line is not an emergency service. Time spent on questions first can cost a life.

Whoever takes the referral

If anyone is in danger now, or serious harm is about to happen:

Tell the referrer to call 000 first.

Say it before you ask any other question. If the referrer cannot call, call 000 yourself and give the address. Do not give advice on how to hold or confine the participant.

Result
Emergency help is on its way before we do anything else.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q3
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Step 2

Whoever takes the referral

Write down the referral in the referrer's own words.

Open FRM-SBS-03 and answer only its referral questions, Q1 to Q14, which serve as the intake record. The clinical sections wait for the Practitioner. Record who referred, when and how. Record who the participant is, where they are and who is at risk. Record what happened and what is being done now. Record whether anyone has used a restrictive practice, and the date it was first used. Say if we would be taking over from another specialist provider. Ask whether the participant knows about the referral. Tell the Service Manager. Use the paper copy of FRM-SBS-03 and FRM-SBS-07 if the system is down.

Result
The Service Manager has the whole referral, and nothing depends on memory.

FRM-SBS-07 Q1 and Q4; FRM-SBS-03 Q1, Q2 and Q4; REG-SBS-01 (participant; referral received; engaged because of a )

Within 1 hour of the referral (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q1, FRM-SBS-07 Q4, FRM-SBS-03 Q1, FRM-SBS-03 Q2, FRM-SBS-03 Q4.

Step 3

Clinical Lead, or a Practitioner the Clinical Lead names

Set the urgency band using Decision table 1.

If you are unsure between two bands, choose the more urgent one. Ask the Clinical Supervisor if you cannot decide. Do not wait for more information before you decide.

Result
Every referral has a band and a reason, so the times that follow are fixed.

FRM-SBS-07 Q2
Time limit
Within 1 business day of the referral, and straight away if step 1 applied (our standard)

Step 4

Service Manager

If the band is "Not immediate" or "Covered by a current plan":

Tell the referrer in writing where the referral goes and why.

Send the referral to PRO-BSP-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure. It sets the assessment, the plan and the steps for taking over from another provider. For a plan we hold, send it to PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure for an early review. Say why this is not an interim plan. Tell the referrer to call again straight away if anyone is in danger or things get worse.

Result
The referral is on the right pathway, and the referrer knows what to do if things get worse.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q6
Time limit
The same business day as step 3 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C1. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q6.

Step 5

Service Manager

Decide whether we can take the referral.

Check three things. A suitable Practitioner can start within the times for the band. A Clinical Supervisor can check the plan before it is issued. Nobody involved has a conflict of interest (POL-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Policy). Name the Practitioner and the Clinical Supervisor. Check the Practitioner's suitability on the record kept under PRO-SBS-01 Behaviour Support in the NDIS Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support); the Commission's outcome is suitable, not suitable or unable to decide, and it records no capability level. Do not wait for a signed service agreement. If the participant's NDIS plan has no behaviour support funding, tell the Chief Executive the same day. They decide whether to start the interim plan, and record the decision.

Result
We accept only a referral we can meet in time, with named people.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q6 and Q7; REG-SBS-01 (Practitioner; Clinical Supervisor)
Time limit
The same business day as the referral for danger now, and within 2 business days of the referral for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2, Policy C4. Written on: FRM-SBS-03 Q6, FRM-SBS-03 Q7.

Step 6

Service Manager

If we cannot take the referral:

Tell the referrer in writing that we cannot take it.

Give the reason and the date. Give the names of other specialist behaviour support providers you know of. Ask the participant's support coordinator or plan manager, if there is one, to help. Where a restrictive practice has been used and is likely to continue, remind the referrer of the provider's own duty. It must take all reasonable steps to have an interim plan made within 1 month of the first use. A comprehensive plan is due within 6 months (Rules, s 11(2), s 12(2) and s 13(2)).

Result
The referrer can act the same day with another provider.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q6
Time limit
The same business day as the decision at step 5 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q6.

Step 7

Service Manager

Accept the referral in writing and record the engagement date.

Tell the referrer the band, the Practitioner's name and the dates for the risk evaluation and the interim plan. The engagement date is the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, which is the day you accept in writing, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used and led to the referral, whichever is earlier (our standard; POL-SBS-07 Ground rule 4). Say in the acceptance that it is the start date for developing the plan for the purposes of the Rules, s 19. Where the first use was before our acceptance, the clocks are already running: tell the Clinical Lead and the Chief Executive the same day if the interim plan due date is less than 5 business days away or has passed. Open the plan row in REG-SBS-01 as an interim plan. Enter the engagement date and both legal due dates, worked out as PRO-BSP-03 sets. Set our own target date for the interim plan from Decision table 3.

Result
Both clocks are running, and the plan row and the target date exist.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q7; FRM-SBS-03 Q3 and Q5; REG-SBS-01 (plan number and version; plan type; engaged on; interim plan due; comprehensive plan due)
Time limit
The same business day as the decision at step 5 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C2, Policy C5. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q7, FRM-SBS-03 Q3, FRM-SBS-03 Q5.

Step 8

Service Manager

If a regulated restrictive practice has been used:

Tell the provider that used the practice the dates that apply to it.

Where the use is likely to continue, that provider has its own limits. It must take all reasonable steps to have an interim plan made within 1 month of the first use. A comprehensive plan is due within 6 months (Rules, s 11(2), s 12(2) and s 13(2)). Those dates can end before ours. Give them in writing with the first use date from FRM-SBS-03. Tell the Clinical Lead if the 1 month date is less than 5 business days away.

Result
The provider knows its own limits, and we know if ours must be faster.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q5
Time limit
On the day you accept the referral (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C5. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q5.

Step 9

Warning. Phone advice to use a restrictive practice, with no plan and no authorisation, can make that use unauthorised. The provider that uses it may then have to report it as a reportable incident.

Practitioner

Check with the lead implementing provider what is keeping people safe today.

Ask what workers do now when the behaviour happens. Ask whether anyone is hurt and whether any restrictive practice is in use. Ask who is on shift tonight. Agree who phones whom if things get worse. Point them to the emergency steps in the participant's support plan (FRM-SUP-02 Participant Support Plan Template). If the participant has no provider yet, do this with the family or carers who support them. Do not tell anyone to use a restrictive practice.

Result
People are as safe as we can make them until the plan is issued, and the provider has our number.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q8
Time limit
The same day as the engagement date for danger now, and within 1 business day of it for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C3. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q8.

Involve the participant

Step 10

Practitioner

Tell the participant what is happening and how they can take part.

Use their way of communicating (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form). Say who we are, who referred them and what we will do. Offer an independent advocate and a support person of their choice. Ask how and when they want to talk.

Result
The participant knows what is happening and has chosen how to take part.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q9 and Q14
Time limit
Within 1 business day of the engagement date for danger now, and within 3 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C6. Written on: FRM-SBS-03 Q9, FRM-SBS-03 Q14.

Step 11

Practitioner

Ask for consent to collect, use and share information for this plan.

Presume the participant can decide, with support (POL-RGT-03 Independence and Informed Choice Policy). Where someone else holds legal authority, see the order or instrument and note what it covers. Ask which family, carers and others we may talk to, and which we may give the plan and to. Write down each person, including every "no". Use FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form.

Result
We know who can decide, and who we may talk to and share with.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q10 to Q13; REG-SBS-01 (who decides; consent to assess and to collect information; consent)
Time limit
At the first conversation with the participant (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C6, Policy C7, Policy C13. Written on: FRM-SBS-03 Q10, FRM-SBS-03 Q11, FRM-SBS-03 Q12, FRM-SBS-03 Q13.

Evaluate the risk

Step 12

Practitioner

Ask the participant how they see the behaviour and the risk.

Ask what happens, what helps, what makes it worse and what worries them. Ask what they want. If they do not use words, watch how they respond and ask the people who know their signs. Let a support person stay. Write their words or signs, not yours. If they choose not to take part, respect that, record why and offer again when you show them the draft.

Result
The participant's view is part of the risk evaluation.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q9
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C6, Policy C8. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q9.

Step 13

Practitioner

Hold the risk evaluation with each implementing provider.

Include the manager and a worker who knows the participant well. Ask what the behaviour looks like, when it happens and what workers do. Ask who else is at risk. Ask for their records from the last 3 months: incidents, injuries, restrictive practice use and behaviour data. Note who gave you each record and when. If the participant has no provider yet, hold it with the family or carers who will carry out the plan. Ask the referrer or the support coordinator to find a provider before the plan is issued.

Result
Each implementing provider has taken part and given us what it holds.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q10 and Q11; REG-SBS-01 (implementing providers consulted)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C7, Policy C8. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q10, FRM-SBS-07 Q11.

Step 14

Practitioner

Gather what other people and services already know.

Ask the family, carers or guardian the participant agreed to. Ask the services involved, such as the treating doctor, a mental health service, a hospital, the police, a school or a day service. Read earlier assessments and plans. Note what worked and what did not. Record each source and the date.

Result
The plan builds on what is known and does not repeat a strategy that failed.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q12 and Q13; REG-SBS-01 (sources used)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C7. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q12, FRM-SBS-07 Q13.

Step 15

Practitioner

Describe the behaviour and what is happening around it.

Say what it looks like, how often it happens, how long it lasts and how strong it is. Say what comes before, during and after it. Say when the risk is lower and when it is higher. Write your working view of why it happens, and mark it as a working view. The full functional behaviour assessment comes with the comprehensive plan.

Result
Everyone reads the same description, and the plan rests on a stated view.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q14 and Q15
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C8, Policy C9. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q14, FRM-SBS-07 Q15.

Step 16

Practitioner

Rate the risk to the participant and the risk to others.

Write one line for each person or group who could be harmed. Include the participant, other participants, workers, family and the public. Say how each could be harmed, including by the response to the behaviour. Rate each as low, medium, high or extreme, using the scale at Q16. Rate the risk as it is now, before any new strategy.

Result
The risks are written down and ranked, so the plan knows what to deal with first.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q16 and Q17; REG-SBS-01 (risk of harm)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C8. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q16, FRM-SBS-07 Q17.

Step 17

Practitioner

Ask the participant's treating practitioner to check for a health cause.

Pain, illness, poor sleep, hunger, a medicine change, and trouble with hearing or sight can all drive behaviour. You do not diagnose. Do not advise a change of medicine, which only the prescriber decides. Ask only with consent. Note who you asked and when. Then write the date you finished the risk evaluation.

Result
A health cause is looked for alongside the plan, and the evaluation has a finish date.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q1 and Q18; REG-SBS-01 (health review; interim risk evaluation)
Time limit
Within 1 business day of step 16 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C8. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q18, FRM-SBS-07 Q1.

Check any restrictive practice

Step 18

Practitioner

If a regulated restrictive practice is in use, or is likely to be needed:

List each regulated restrictive practice.

For each one write the type: seclusion, chemical, mechanical, physical or environmental restraint. Write exactly what is done, which provider does it, where, and what behaviour it responds to. Examples are a locked cupboard or fridge, a bed rail, a sedating medicine given to manage behaviour, and holding a person still. If you are unsure whether something is a restrictive practice, treat it as one and ask the Clinical Supervisor. For a medicine, name the prescriber and the date of their last review. Never copy a dose.

Result
Every practice in use or proposed is named.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q19; REG-SBS-01 (restrictive practices in the plan)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C10. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q19.

Step 19

Practitioner

If a regulated restrictive practice is in use, or is likely to be needed:

Check whether each practice is authorised.

Find the state or territory process in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. Ask the provider for the authorisation: who gave it, from when to when, any short term approval, and who consented. A state or territory may prohibit a practice. If it does, the practice cannot go in the plan (Rules, s 8). A single emergency use needs no authorisation first (Rules, s 9(2)(a)), but any use without authorisation is a reportable incident for the provider (NDIS Act 2013, s 73Z(4)(f)), and the plan never writes such a practice as allowed. Check on the NDIS Provider Register that the provider is registered for the supports it gives (Practice Standards Rules, s 7(2)).

Result
The authorisation status of each practice is known and written down.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q20; REG-SBS-01 (authorisation)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 4 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C10. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q20.

Step 20

Practitioner

If a regulated restrictive practice is in use, or is likely to be needed:

Decide for each practice whether it goes in the plan, using Decision table 2.

Test each practice against the Rules (s 21(3)). It must be a last resort and the least restrictive response. It must be in proportion to the risk, for the shortest time, and reduce the risk. Write why it passes or fails. Write how it will be reduced and ended. Write what the participant will learn or do instead (Rules, s 20(3)(a) and s 21(4)). Ask the Clinical Supervisor if you are unsure.

Result
Each practice is in, out, or in as "not yet authorised: must not be used", with reasons.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q21 and Q22; REG-SBS-01 (authorisation; reduction strategy)
Time limit
Within 3 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 5 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C10. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q21, FRM-SBS-07 Q22.

Step 21

Practitioner

If a restrictive practice stays in the draft plan after step 20:

Give the participant and their family, carers, guardian or other relevant person the details of the intention to include the practice.

Use a format they can use: spoken, written, pictures or an interpreter. Explain what the practice is and why it is proposed. Explain the risks, the alternatives you looked at and how it will end. Ask what they think and write it down. Keep a written note of what you gave them. Record the full consultation on FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record, as PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) sets out for an interim plan.

Result
They know before the plan is final, in a way they understand, and have been asked.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q23; FRM-SBS-02 (the consultation record); REG-SBS-01 (consultation and notice of intention)
Time limit
Before the plan is finalised (statutory: Rules, s 20(4)). Use the shorter notice that PRO-SBS-02 allows where the risk is immediate, and write the reason down (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C11. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q23.

Write and check the plan

Step 22

Practitioner

Agree the interim strategies with the participant and the implementing providers.

Start with prevention: changes to the setting, routine, communication and supports. Then what to teach or offer instead, and the community and skill building chances the participant will get. Then what workers do while the behaviour is happening, in order, and what they never do. Then what they do afterwards for the participant and anyone hurt. Last, what they record, how it reaches us, and who to call. Say who does each step and how we will know it is followed. Where a hospital, a mental health service or the police are involved, agree with them what each will do in a crisis.

Result
Providers have agreed strategies that put proactive steps first.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q24 to Q26
Time limit
Within 3 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 6 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C9. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q24, FRM-SBS-07 Q25, FRM-SBS-07 Q26.

Step 23

Practitioner

Write the interim plan on the Commissioner's approved form.

Get the current form through FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record. Use it, or another form that the Rules, s 23(1), allow and that holds every required item, for every interim plan, with or without a restrictive practice. Complete the cover sheet as you go. Put in the behaviour, the risk, the strategies from step 22 and your working view of why. Put in each practice that passed Decision table 2, with its authorisation details and, for one not yet authorised, the words "Not yet authorised. Must not be used" and what happens until authorisation is granted. The plan on the approved form carries the medication details the form requires; FRM-SBS-07 carries none. Check the draft against the Commission's Interim Behaviour Support Plan Checklist (October 2025), items 12 to 20: brief and usable, evaluates the risk, no functional behaviour assessment, changes within the environment, and for each practice what, when, why, how and by whom. Write in plain words that a worker on a first shift can follow. Set the start date. The end date is the comprehensive plan's due date.

Result
A draft plan exists on the approved form, and the cover sheet is open.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 (the plan type, form used and practices); REG-SBS-01 (version and why it was made; form used; plan content check)
Time limit
Within 3 business days of the engagement date for danger now, and within 6 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C9.

Step 24

Practitioner

Go through the draft plan with the participant.

Use their way of communicating, with the people they chose. Give them the draft in a form they understand. Ask what they think, what they would change and whether it feels right. Change what you can. Say why where you cannot. Write their view in their words on the cover sheet.

Result
The participant has seen the draft and been heard before it is final.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 (the participant's view and when the draft was given); REG-SBS-01 (participant's view of the plan; draft given to participant)
Time limit
Within 1 business day of step 23 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C6.

Step 25

Practitioner

Send the draft plan to each implementing provider for consideration and acceptance.

Ask each provider to say in writing whether it can follow the plan, what it would change and who will lead. Record each reply on the cover sheet. Phone any provider that has not replied by the limit. PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure sets how a reply is answered.

Result
Each provider has considered the plan, and any problem is known before the plan is issued.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 (each provider's answer); REG-SBS-01 (implementing providers consulted; acceptance)
Time limit
Send it the day you finish step 24. Replies are due within 1 business day for danger now and within 2 for urgent (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C7.

Step 26

Clinical Supervisor

Check the draft plan and the risk evaluation.

Check that every risk to the participant and to others is dealt with. Check that the strategies are proactive first. Check that each restrictive practice is named, tested and shows its authorisation status, and that no practice without authorisation or an is written as allowed. Check that the participant's view is in, the words are plain and the dates are right. Sign the Clinical Supervisor check on the cover sheet. Accept the plan, or return it with the changes needed. In a sole practitioner provider, the external Clinical Supervisor does this check.

Result
A second qualified person has agreed that the plan is safe to issue.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 (the Clinical Supervisor's check); REG-SBS-01 (Clinical Supervisor)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the replies at step 25, and inside the plan's issue date (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C4, Policy C9.

Step 27

Practitioner

Finalise the plan and record its version and dates.

Finalise only after the Clinical Supervisor has accepted the plan. Make any changes the providers asked for first. The plan is finalised on the date you sign it. That date is the date the plan is in force and issued. Record the version number, the start date and the end date. The end date, and the plan's review date, is the comprehensive plan's due date, never 12 months.

Result
The interim plan exists, with its dates, and everyone can tell which version is current.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 (the version and the date finalised); REG-SBS-01 (current version and date finalised)
Time limit
By the interim plan due date: 5 business days after the engagement date for danger now, and 10 for urgent (our standard). Never later than 1 month after it where a practice has been used (statutory: Rules, s 19(2)(a)), or is likely (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C5, Policy C9.

Give out the plan and lodge it

Step 28

Practitioner

Give the participant their copy of the plan and explain it.

Do this before anyone else is told. Use the format they chose: spoken, plain words, pictures, large print or their language. Offer STA-BSP-01 Behaviour Support and Restrictive Practices: Plain Summary with it. Tell them how to ask for a change and how to complain (POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy). Give a copy to the person with legal authority too, if there is one. Record it as PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure sets out.

Result
The participant knows what the plan says and what they can do about it.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 (the participant's handover); REG-SBS-01 (date given to implementers)
Time limit
Within 1 business day of the plan being issued, and before step 30 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C6.

Step 29

Warning. A false or misleading statement to the Commission is an offence under the Criminal Code (Part 7.4).

Service Manager

If the plan contains a regulated restrictive practice:

Lodge the plan with the Commissioner in the form and manner the Commissioner requires.

Lodge it even where the state or territory needs no authorisation, or authorisation is not yet in place (Rules, s 24(2)). Attach what the Commissioner asks for. Keep the Commission's acknowledgement. Write the date, who lodged it and the reference on the cover sheet. Tell each implementing provider the date. A sole practitioner lodges the plan themselves.

Result
The Commissioner holds the plan, and we have the reference.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 (the lodgement date and reference); REG-SBS-01 (lodgement required; lodgement due; Commission lodgement)
Time limit
Within 5 business days of finalising the plan, as REG-SBS-01 (lodgement due) works it out (our standard). The Rules say as soon as practicable (statutory: Rules, s 24(1))

Carries out: Policy C12.

Give advice and guidance

Step 30

Practitioner

Coach each implementing provider in carrying out the plan.

Give each provider the issued plan and the one page point-of-care card, and brief its manager, within 1 business day of issue. Then follow the handover and coaching steps of PRO-SBS-03 within its interim handover clock of 2 business days from issue. Meet the manager and the workers who will carry it out, including night and weekend workers. Where a worker cannot be met in that time, the provider's supervisor goes through the card with them at the start of their first shift, trains and observes them against the plan and confirms it to you in writing, as PRO-SBS-03 sets. Cover what the plan says and why. Cover each step, what never to do, how to record and who to call. Where a restrictive practice is in the plan, cover its authorisation status, what the plan says about a practice not yet authorised, and the provider's duty to lodge evidence of authorisation with the Commissioner. Cover its monthly reports, which are every 2 weeks under a short term approval (Rules, s 9(2)(b) and s 14(1)). Ask workers to say the steps back in their own words.

Result
Each provider can carry out the plan, and gaps are known on day one.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q27; FRM-SBS-04 (the handover and coaching records); REG-SBS-01 (date given to implementers; handover and training)
Time limit
The issued plan, the card and the manager briefing within 1 business day of issue. Handover and coaching complete within 2 business days of issue, the interim handover clock in PRO-SBS-03 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C13. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q27.

Step 31

Practitioner

If the participant, or the person with legal authority, agreed that we may give guidance to their :

Give guidance to the people they named.

Check each person's name against REG-SBS-01 (consent: what may be shared) before you share anything. Give only what they need to support the participant under the plan. Do not share the participant's other records. Show them what to do and who to call. Record it on FRM-SBS-04.

Result
The people close to the participant can help, and nobody is told without consent.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q27; FRM-SBS-04 (the support network's handover); REG-SBS-01 (date given to implementers)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the plan being issued, the interim handover clock in PRO-SBS-03 (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C13. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q27.

Follow up, change and close

Step 32

Practitioner

Make the first check on how the plan is working.

Ask each implementing provider whether workers are following it and whether the behaviour has changed. Ask whether any restrictive practice was used, and whether the use matched the plan. Ask what data they have and what is hard. Ask the participant too. Add a line to the follow-up log. Fix anything small the same day.

Result
We know whether the plan works in practice, and any problem is found in the first week.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q28
Time limit
Within 7 days of the plan being issued (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C14. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q28.

Step 33

Practitioner

Start the monthly checks on the plan under PRO-SBS-04.

Open the first monitoring record on FRM-SBS-05 Behaviour Support Plan Review Record. Set the next check no more than 1 month after the plan was issued, which is the cycle PRO-SBS-04 sets for an interim plan. PRO-SBS-04 sets every step of each check from then on.

Result
The interim plan has a monthly check with a date.
Record
FRM-SBS-05 (the first monitoring check); REG-SBS-01 (next monitoring check and review due)
Time limit
On the day of the first check (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C14.

Step 34

Practitioner

If the plan is not working, a new risk has appeared or a practice has changed:

Start an early review of the plan under PRO-SBS-04.

Open FRM-SBS-05 and choose early review. Change the plan only through that review. Where a restrictive practice is in the plan, lodge the new version (step 29). Tell everyone who had guidance and give them the new version (steps 30 and 31). Keep every earlier version.

Result
The plan in use is always the current version, and everyone has it.
Record
FRM-SBS-05 (the early review record); REG-SBS-01 (version and why it was made; type of last review)
Time limit
The same business day where someone is at risk, and within 5 business days of the trigger otherwise (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C14.

Step 35

Practitioner

If a regulated restrictive practice is in the plan, or the need for behaviour support continues:

Move the work on to the comprehensive plan.

Follow PRO-BSP-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure. Give it the risk evaluation and the follow-up log. Do not ask the participant for the same information again. The comprehensive plan is due within 6 months of the engagement date where a practice has been used (statutory: Rules, s 19(2)(b)). We apply the same limit where a practice is likely (our standard). Tell the participant and the providers the due date.

Result
The interim plan has a successor with a date.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q29; FRM-SBS-03 (the assessment report is the next record); REG-SBS-01 (comprehensive plan due)
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the plan being issued (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C5, Policy C14. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q29.

Step 36

Practitioner

End the interim plan and record why.

End it on the day the comprehensive plan is issued, so there is no gap. Or end it when you, the participant and the providers agree that the immediate need is over. Set the end date. Tell the participant and each provider the same day.

Result
The interim plan is closed, and nobody is left without a plan they need.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q30; REG-SBS-01 (status; closed)
Time limit
On the day the comprehensive plan is issued, or within 2 business days of agreeing that the need is over (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C14. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q30.

Keep the clocks

Step 37

Service Manager

Check every open interim plan against its due dates.

Open REG-SBS-01. Look at the legal dates (interim plan due; comprehensive plan due), the lodgement due date and the next monitoring check. Then open each open FRM-SBS-07 and read our target date at Q7. Look for an interim plan due within 2 business days. Look for a comprehensive plan due within 30 days. Look for a first check or a monthly check that is overdue. Look for a plan with a restrictive practice that is not yet lodged. Note each check in the review log kept with the register.

Result
No limit is missed without someone senior knowing.
Record
FRM-SBS-07 Q7; REG-SBS-01 (interim plan due; comprehensive plan due; lodgement due; next monitoring check and review due)
Time limit
Every business day until a danger now plan is issued, then at the start of each week for every open plan (our standard)

Carries out: Policy C5, Policy C14. Written on: FRM-SBS-07 Q7.

6Decision

Decision table 1: Urgency band

Write a new interim plan only if no current plan exists or the existing plan does not manage the risk. Otherwise send it to PRO-BSP-03 for the takeover steps (step 4)

Decision table 2: A restrictive practice in the plan

The plan says what happens until authorisation is granted: the proactive and response strategies used instead, and that if the practice is used in an emergency to prevent serious harm the provider must notify the NDIS Commission as a reportable incident and tell us within 1 business day. 7If it goes wrong

  • The participant, or the person with legal authority, will not consent. Explain what it means. Offer an independent advocate. Tell the Clinical Supervisor the same day. Go on with the collection and consultation that the Rules require for a plan containing a restrictive practice (Rules, s 20(3)), collect only what the plan needs, and record the refusal and what was collected despite it (POL-SBS-07 Ground rule 8). Keep the safety arrangements from step 9 going. Ask again after 10 business days if they agree (our standard).
  • A provider will not take part, or will not send its records. Write each attempt at Q11. Tell the Clinical Supervisor the same day. Go ahead on what you have, and say in the plan what is missing. If the provider will not follow the plan, tell the Commissioner as PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure sets out.
  • The Practitioner is absent or unwell. The Service Manager gives the plan to the cover Practitioner. For danger now that is the same business day, and for urgent within 1 business day. If nobody can start in time, the Service Manager tells the referrer that day and helps them find another specialist behaviour support provider. The engagement date and the due dates do not change.
  • A deadline will be missed. Tell the Clinical Lead and the Chief Executive the same day. Do it at least 7 days before the date where you can. Tell the referrer and each implementing provider in writing, with the new date. Keep the safety arrangements going. Where the limit is set by law, the Chief Executive decides what else must be done. Record the reason on the plan row. Never change a date on the register to hide a late step.
  • The referral shows a restrictive practice used without authorisation, or outside the plan. The provider that used it must treat it as a possible reportable incident. It notifies the Commissioner (Incident Rules, s 16 and s 21). Tell that provider's manager the same day, and start PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). Carry on with this procedure. If our own worker used the practice, complete FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form and follow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure.
  • You suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation. Tell the Service Manager at once and follow PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure.
  • You are worried about a colleague or a manager. Tell the Clinical Supervisor. If it is about the Clinical Supervisor, tell the Clinical Lead. If it is about the Service Manager or the Clinical Lead, tell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive, tell the chair of the governing body, or the independent contact for concerns. For a sole Practitioner's own work, tell the Clinical Supervisor.
  • A provider says it cannot follow the plan. Find out why, with the Clinical Supervisor. Arrange any training under PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure. If the plan still cannot be followed, follow PRO-SBS-04 for telling the Commissioner.
  • The participant or family disagrees with the plan. Write their view in their words on the cover sheet. Change what you can and say why where you cannot. Tell them how to complain (POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy). If the disagreement is about a restrictive practice, the authorisation process of the state or territory decides whether it may be used, not the Practitioner.
  • Systems are down. Use the paper copies of FRM-SBS-03, FRM-SBS-07 and FRM-BSP-02. The Service Manager enters them within 2 business days of the system coming back (our standard).

8Done means

  • The participant has had their say and holds an interim plan in a form they can use. They know how to ask for a change and how to complain.
  • Each implementing provider took part in the risk evaluation, considered the plan, was coached in it and can carry it out. The support network was given guidance only where the participant agreed.
  • The plan was issued by its due date. Where it contains a regulated restrictive practice, it is lodged and the reference is recorded.
  • FRM-SBS-07 is complete and signed. The plan row in REG-SBS-01 is up to date, with the first check, the monthly check and the date the comprehensive plan is due.
  • The interim plan has ended with a reason, and the participant is not left without a plan they need.

9Quick card

133 words
  • If anyone is in danger now, tell the referrer to call 000 first (step 1)
  • Set the urgency band within 1 business day (step 3)
  • Accept in writing and write down the engagement date (step 7)
  • Never tell a provider by phone to use a restrictive practice (step 9)
  • Hold the risk evaluation with the participant and each implementing provider (step 13)
  • Never write a practice as allowed unless its authorisation is shown. A practice not yet authorised is written "must not be used" (step 20)
  • Have the Clinical Supervisor check the plan before it is issued (step 26)
  • Lodge a plan that has a restrictive practice within 5 business days (step 29)
  • Give each provider the issued plan within 1 business day of issue and complete the coaching within 2 (step 30)

questions.hint: Write only what the participant has agreed to share. Say so if they chose to share nothing.

questions.text: What are their home, routines, people and places like day to day, and where or when is the behaviour absent?
questions.hint: Include noise, crowding, light, staffing, rules and changes to routine.

questions.text: What are the participant's unmet needs?
questions.hint: One line each: the need, your evidence, and who could meet it. Include needs for health care, communication, company, activity, choice, safety and sensory comfort.

questions.text: Which behaviours of concern are we assessing, in words an observer could see and hear?
questions.hint: One line each. Describe what happens, not what you think it means.

questions.text: For each behaviour, how often, how long and how intense is it now?
questions.hint: Name the scale you used for intensity and say what each level looks like. Give the period the numbers cover.

questions.text: What are the early warning signs, and how does each behaviour end?
questions.hint: Write what workers can see before it starts and what usually settles it.

questions.text: What is the risk of harm, and to whom?
questions.hint: Say who could be harmed, how likely it is and how serious. Choose low, medium, high or extreme and say why. Our standard scale: low means harm is unlikely and would be minor; medium means harm is possible and would need first aid or cause distress; high means harm is likely, or would need medical treatment; extreme means a risk of death or serious injury, or serious harm happening often. FRM-SBS-07 Interim Behaviour Support Risk Evaluation uses the same scale.

questions.text: What setting events and triggers make each behaviour more likely?
questions.hint: Setting events are things like poor sleep, pain, a change of staff or a crowded day. Triggers are what happens just before.

questions.text: What happens after each behaviour, and what does the participant get or avoid?
questions.hint: Include how others respond.

questions.text: For each behaviour, what does it do for the participant?
questions.hint: Write one summary statement: in this setting, when this happens, the participant does this, and so gets or avoids that. Say how sure you are: tested, likely or unclear.

questions.text: What evidence supports each statement, and what would show it wrong?
questions.hint: Name the data. Say how you tested it, for example by changing one thing and watching.

questions.text: Which other explanations did you rule out or treat?
questions.hint: Pain, illness, medicine effects, sleep, hearing, vision, unmet communication, trauma, noise and change.

questions.text: What skill or behaviour could meet the same need more safely?
questions.hint: One line for each behaviour. It must be a skill the participant can learn and use.

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: Is any restrictive practice used with the participant now, regulated or not?
questions.hint: One line each: what is done, where, who does it, how often and since when. Write "None" if there is none. Examples: a locked room (seclusion); a medicine given to change behaviour (chemical restraint); a lap belt or bed rail used to stop movement (mechanical restraint); holding a person still (physical restraint); a locked cupboard, fridge or gate that stops access (environmental restraint).

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: For each practice, what is its type, its authorisation and its place in a plan?
questions.hint: Type: seclusion, chemical, mechanical, physical, environmental or other. <button type="button" class="term" data-term="authorisation" data-def="the permission a state or territory gives, through its own process, for a regulated restrictive practice. Some states and territories have no such process." data-source="POL-SBS-07">Authorisation</button>: the body, the date and the expiry, or "not needed", or "none". Say whether it is in a current plan and whether that plan was lodged.

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: Did you see any practice that could cause serious harm? What did you do, and when?
questions.hint: For example a restraint that restricts breathing. Give the time you called 000 if anyone was in danger, the time you told the person to stop and the time you told the Service Manager. Record it on our incident system as a witnessed event, tell the implementing provider in writing the same day that it must notify the Commission, and start PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support). The Quality Manager decides whether it is also reportable by us.

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: What does the assessment show about reducing or ending each practice?
questions.hint: Say which unmet need or skill would make the practice unnecessary.

questions.section: Section G: Restrictive practices now in use
questions.text: Do you think a regulated restrictive practice may be needed in the plan?
questions.hint: If yes, stop and tell the Service Manager. Start PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) before the plan is drafted. This report never recommends one.

questions.section: Section H: Other supports and services
questions.text: What other supports and services does the participant use?
questions.hint: One line each: service, what it does, the contact, and what it does when the behaviour happens. Include health, mental health, education, housing, justice, day and community services.

questions.section: Section H: Other supports and services
questions.text: How should these services fit together, and which have agreed to a protocol?
questions.hint: Say what each service and each implementing provider must do, and who tells whom. With the participant's consent, ask each service to agree. Give the date each agreed.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What changes to the environment do you recommend?
questions.hint: Start here: noise, space, light, routine, staff and rules.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What skills should we teach, and what replacement behaviours do you recommend?
questions.hint: Link each to a function in Section F.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What proactive strategies do you recommend?
questions.hint: Think about daily life, communication, routines, relationships, activities and choice.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What response strategies do you recommend for when the behaviour happens?
questions.hint: Strategies that keep people safe and help the participant settle. Never a restrictive practice.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What evidence supports each recommended strategy?
questions.hint: One line for each strategy: the function it answers, the assessment data it rests on, and the practice <button type="button" class="term" data-term="guidance" data-def="teaching and coaching on how to carry out the plan, with a check that it was understood." data-source="POL-SBS-07">guidance</button> or research behind it, such as the Commission's behaviour support guidance or a recognised positive behaviour support framework. Never include a strategy that does not answer a function.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What data should each implementing provider collect, how often, and how will we check the plan is followed?
questions.hint: Name the form, the measure and the day each month it reaches us.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: What training do the implementing providers need?
questions.hint: Name the topic and who needs it. PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure arranges it.

questions.section: Section I: Recommendations for the plan
questions.text: How can the participant take part in community activities and learn new skills that reduce any need for a restrictive practice?
questions.hint: Give at least one activity or skill.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: When and how did you go through the findings with the participant, and what did they say?
questions.hint: Give the date, the format, who helped, their response and any disagreement in their words.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: Which implementing providers were consulted and given the findings, and what did each say?
questions.hint: Only with the participant's consent. One line each: provider, date and what they said.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: Was an automated or AI tool used for any part of this report?
questions.hint: If yes, name the tool, say what it was used for and what information went in. Nothing that identifies the participant may go into a tool that POL-TEC-01 Artificial Intelligence and Automated Tools Policy has not approved.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: When will we look at this assessment again, and what would make us look sooner?
questions.hint: No more than 12 months after the report is finalised. Sooner for a new setting, a health change, a loss or a new restrictive practice.

questions.section: Section J: Sharing, tools and review
questions.text: Did the Clinical Supervisor check this report? Give the date and the outcome.
questions.hint: The <button type="button" class="term" data-term="Clinical Supervisor" data-def="an experienced Practitioner who checks the Practitioner's work and supports their practice." data-source="POL-SBS-07">Clinical Supervisor</button> answers. The outcome is accepted, or returned with the changes needed.

form.intro:
Use this template to write the assessment report. It shows what we found out about the participant and why, and what we recommend for their plan.

The Practitioner completes Sections B to J, and nobody else signs the clinical content. Section A is completed by the Service Manager from the plan row in REG-SBS-01 (PRO-BSP-03 steps 1 to 5), and the Practitioner copies the plan number into the report. Workers, family members and managers give information and records. They do not write findings. Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this template. An implementing provider does not write assessment reports; it supplies behaviour records (FRM-BSP-04 Behaviour Record) to the Practitioner.

Start the report on the day the referral is logged. Fill it in as the assessment goes. Finalise it within 49 days of the engagement date (our standard).

Have ready:

  • the referral and the service agreement
  • the participant's communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form) and their consent record (FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form)
  • earlier plans and assessments, and the data from each implementing provider.

What happens next: the Clinical Supervisor checks the report within 3 . The Practitioner goes through it with the participant within 5 business days of the check. The Service Manager copies the answers marked for REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register to the plan row within 2 business days.

"Behaviour Support Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to understand the participant and why they behave as they do, so we can write a plan that helps them. It holds sensitive information about their health, history and behaviour.

The Practitioner, the Clinical Supervisor and the Service Manager read it. We ask for information only from the people and services the participant agreed to (Q12), except that the law requires us to consult the providers who may use a restrictive practice; we tell the participant first and share only what they need. We share the report only with the people they agreed to (Q13). We give a plan with a regulated restrictive practice, and this report with it, to the NDIS Commissioner, as the Behaviour Support Rules require.

The participant can see this report and ask us to correct it. They can ask us to stop at any time. FRM-INF-02 Request to Access or Correct Personal Information Form is the form to ask. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.
form.after:
1. The Practitioner gives the finished report to the Clinical Supervisor the same day (PRO-BSP-03 step 15).
  2. The Clinical Supervisor checks it within 3 business days and signs the sign-off block (PRO-BSP-03 step 16).
  3. The Practitioner goes through it with the participant within 5 business days of the check (PRO-BSP-03 step 17).
  4. The Service Manager copies each answer marked for REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register to the plan row within 2 business days (PRO-BSP-03 step 30).
  5. The report is filed on the participant's file. We share it only as Q13 says.
  6. A sole Practitioner files the report and updates the register themselves. The outside Clinical Supervisor does the check.

The plan itself is written on the Commissioner's approved form (FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record). This record does not replace it.

This record authorises no restrictive practice. Only the authorisation process of the state or territory can do that.

Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this record. A provider that only implements plans uses FRM-BSP-08 Interim Behaviour Support Engagement Record.

This record holds only what is new in an interim plan. The referral, the engagement date, the and the consent are on FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template. The cover sheet FRM-BSP-02 holds the plan's checks, acceptance and lodgement. FRM-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Handover and Training Record holds the handover. FRM-SBS-05 Behaviour Support Plan Review Record holds the monthly checks. Do not write the same answer twice.

Who completes it:

  • Section A: whoever takes the referral starts it. The and the Service Manager finish it.
  • Sections B to G: the Practitioner, as each step of PRO-SBS-06 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) is done.
  • Q30: the Practitioner records it, and the Service Manager closes the record.

Answer the questions in section D only when the answer to Q4 shows a practice. Each question in section D is answered once for each practice.

Have ready: the referral and any earlier plans. Have the participant's communication preferences (FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form). Have their consent record (FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form). Have the authorisation schedule in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.

Three answers open the next step. A band of "Not immediate" or "Covered by a current plan" at Q2 sends the referral to another pathway. A practice at Q4 opens section D and the lodgement duty. A band of "Danger now" opens the 000 call at Q3.

What happens next: the Service Manager copies the answers marked for REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register to the plan row. This is within 2 business days of the stage, as the register's entry rules set. PRO-SBS-06 sets every step.

When systems are down, use the paper copy. Enter it in the system within 2 business days of the system coming back (our standard).
form.privacy:
We collect this information to work out how to keep a participant and other people safe. We use it to write an interim plan and to help those who carry it out. Some of it is health information, which is sensitive.

The Practitioner, the Clinical Supervisor and the Service Manager read this record. We give the providers who carry out the plan the parts they need. We share with a participant's only what the participant agreed to. We a plan that contains a regulated restrictive practice with the NDIS Commissioner, because the law requires it.

If you are the participant, you can ask to see this record and ask us to correct it. You can have an advocate with you. You can tell us you disagree, and we will write it down in your words. To complain, use POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store this record and how long we keep it.
form.after:

columns.name: Plan number and version
columns.meaning: The one number that follows this plan version through every record
